subject: QuantumWave - Dedicated GPU pool sizing and commit structure
messages:
From: Maya Rao <maya@quantumwave.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@quantumwave.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity question for real-time annotator

Hi Chloe —

Thanks for the demo last week. We want to move from proof-of-concept to a committed Dedicated pool for our real-time annotation pipeline. A few specifics to help sizing:
- Expected steady-state QPS for token-generation requests: ~120 requests/sec. Typical prompt -> response average tokens generated: 160 tokens.
- Average input prompt length (context): 1.2k tokens (we send several documents in the prompt).
- P95 latency target: <= 250ms for short responses (<=64 tokens); for full responses we can accept up to 800ms.
- Concurrency pattern: bursts to 250 concurrent requests for 30–90s every hour; baseline concurrency ~30.
- Model mix: 70% open-llama-70b-quant (fp16), 30% gpt3.5-ish lighter variant for cheap embeddings/reranking.

We also want guidance on committed monthly GPU hours vs. burst credits and an outline of discount tiers for a 12-month commit. Can you recommend pool size (GPU count/type), throughput guarantees, and an MPA sketch?

I'll attach the current workload CSV.

Thanks,
Maya
CTO, QuantumWave

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rao <maya@quantumwave.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question for real-time annotator

Hi Maya — appreciate the details, that's very helpful. I did a quick first-pass sizing with Soojin and Karthik; attaching a high-level workbook with assumptions. Quick summary up-front:

- Recommended baseline: 8x A40-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated pool to cover steady-state 120 QPS with your model mix and KV cache strategy.
- Autoscale burst buffer: additional burst capacity equivalent to ~4 GPUs (pre-warmed hot standbys or burst credits) to hit the 250 concurrent spike target with acceptable P95.
- Commitment tier: for 12-month reserved commit we suggest a "guaranteed 8 GPUs + 50% burst credits" structure; equivalent monthly commit ~5.5 GPU-months (since bursts are credit-backed), with a reserved discount tier starting at 22% off hosted rates.

Assumptions included in the workbook: token-generation throughput per GPU at 160 tokens/req, average sequence length accounting, KV cache hit rate ~35% for repeated context, and a 25% safety buffer for peaks. Soojin will add notes on latency tuning (quantization / batching knobs).

Can you confirm the percent of requests that are short (<64 tokens) vs long (>256 tokens)? Also, do you expect model mix to shift toward larger models in next 6 months? That affects GPU type recommendations.

Next steps: if the numbers look close to what you expect, Karthik can put together a pricing worksheet with discount tiers and a draft MPA for legal.

Best,
Chloe
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: quantumwave_workload_breakdown.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rao <maya@quantumwave.ai>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QuantumWave - Dedicated GPU pool sizing and commit structure

Maya — following up with pricing considerations and a few alternative packaging options. High level:

Option A (Predictable):
- Commit: 8 guaranteed GPUs (A40-equivalent) — billed monthly as reserved capacity.
- Burst: additional 50% burst credits (4 GPU-equivalents) usable for spikes; bursts deducted from monthly credit pool.
- Discount: 25% off-list for a 12-month commit at this level.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime on reserved capacity; latency SLOs subject to model mix and concurrency.
- Pros: predictable unit economics, easier internal chargebacks.

Option B (Flexible + lower commit):
- Commit: 5 guaranteed GPUs + access to 5 GPUs in a shared overflow pool with pay-as-you-go for overflow usage.
- Discount: 15% on committed portion; overflow billed at hosted rate with a 10% volume discount.
- Pros: lower commitment, smoother initial ramp.

We recommend Option A if you need strict P95 latency targets and want to simplify forecasting. Option B if you prefer lower upfront commitment and expect model mix changes.

Questions for you to finalize:
1) Target monthly committed spend range (helps us pick discount band).
2) Is legal okay with a 12-month MPA and a quarterly usage review clause?

I'll draft a formal pricing worksheet and MPA template once we land on preferred packaging.

- Karthik
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_pricing_options.pdf

From: Maya Rao <maya@quantumwave.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QuantumWave - Dedicated GPU pool sizing and commit structure

Thanks — helpful options. A few clarifications from our side:
- Short vs long split: ~55% short (<64 tokens), ~35% medium (64-256), ~10% long (>256) today. We plan to shift ~20% of traffic to a larger model for higher-fidelity responses in Q1; that would change burst compute needs.
- Commitment budget: we're targeting $55k–$75k/month committed spend for year 1 if the economics match.
- Legal: 12-month MPA is fine; would like a 30-day review window and a built-in option to increase committed GPUs mid-term (with pro-rated pricing).

Two asks before we sign: 1) a short appendix listing how we’d handle an unplanned surge beyond burst credits (failover to hosted model at slightly higher latency/cost?), and 2) a sample monthly usage dashboard view so our ops team can reconcile chargebacks.

If you can send updated numbers with the 12-month 25% discount (Option A), and a pro-forma MPA with the 30-day review and mid-term scale clause, we'll take to procurement.

-Maya
